inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero: Brenntag's LTIP is cash-settled virtual shares (FY2025 AR note, provision EUR 8.9m, p.~13564) expensed inside operating costs; the first equity-settled awards granted June 2026 are covered by treasury-share repurchases with no dilution (H1 2026 report note 6). No cash-flow SBC add-back exists, so owner FCF = reported FCF less lease principal only.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 EUR 0 (FY2024 EUR 250.1m, FY2023 EUR 496.2m under the EUR 750m programme). Flat 144.4m count is a modelling convention, not currently funded by repurchases.
inputs.share_count_basis: 144,385,372 shares in issue (H1 2026 report; no treasury shares at FY2025, diluted EPS = basic EPS). Held FLAT: SBC is nil/cash-settled and the June 2026 equity awards are backed by repurchased shares.
inputs.last_fcf_derivation: FY2025 OCF 966.7 - capex 293.0 = reported FCF 673.7 (CSV basis); less lease principal repayments 149.1 (lease treatment B) = 524.6 owner FCF. Brenntag's own 'free cash flow' of EUR 940.8m is pre-tax and pre-interest (operating EBITDA - capex +/- WC - lease payments) and is NOT comparable.
inputs.net_debt_derivation: H1 2026 report table 1.10: financial liabilities 3,021 (syndicated loan 163, banks 181, Schuldschein 493, bonds 2028/29/31/32 2,111, derivatives 20, other 53) less cash 509 = 2,512. Lease liabilities 588 excluded because lease cash cost is charged inside the flows (treatment B). Company-defined net financial liabilities incl. leases = 3,100. June balance carries the seasonal/price-driven H1 working-capital build of EUR 460m.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-denominated flows discounted at a EUR WACC: 10y Bund ~2.8%, ERP 5.5%, beta ~1.05 -> cost of equity ~8.6%; pre-tax cost of debt ~3.5% (Oct-2025 EUR 600m 2031 bond at 3.375%, BBB+/Baa2) -> ~2.6% after tax; market-value weights ~75% equity (EUR 9.1bn cap) / 25% debt (EUR 3.1bn) -> 7.1%, rounded up to 7.5% for a mid-cap cyclical. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality is charged in the flows via scenario weighting, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. Full lease cash cost (FY2025 principal 149.1 + lease interest 26.2 = 175.3, 1.16% of revenue; H1 2026 90) deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities (588 at 30-Jun-2026) EXCLUDED from net debt; D&A path is ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 D&A ex impairments 420.7 = 358.2 PP&E/ROU + 62.5 intangibles, less ROU depreciation 155.4 = 265.3, 1.75% of revenue) so cash-tax EBIT is not charged for leases twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; NCI equity (total equity 4,348.6 less shareholders' equity 4,314.1 = EUR 34.5m at FY2025; NCI profit share EUR 5.1m) deducted once in the equity bridge.
inputs.ebitda_basis: Model EBITDA is the CSV 'EBITDA' line, i.e. operating EBITDA AFTER net special items (FY2025: operating EBITDA 1,287.5, special items -106.5 incl. legal-risk costs 32.2 and strategy-project costs 40.5). Special items recur every year at Brenntag (FY2024 -111.4, H1 2026 -67) so they are treated as a real cost. Post-IFRS16 margin on this basis FY2019-FY2025: 7.9, 8.6, 7.8, 9.2, 9.0, 8.4, 8.0 -> mid-cycle ~8.4%.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, non-US cyclical -> owner-fcf.md + adaptations a1/b/c/e/f). FY2025 is a cyclical trough (management: longest chemical downturn in 20+ years; EPS 1.83 vs 3.71; EBITDA margin 7.96%, lowest post-IFRS16) so the margin path is anchored to the FY2026 operating-EBITDA guidance of EUR 1,350-1,450m (raised twice; H1 2026 op. EBITDA 770, +16% cc; Q2 +38.8%) and glides to a mid-cycle 8.4-8.7% rather than extrapolating FY2025. Capital Markets Day 12-Nov-2026 (new CEO Birgersson's strategy, mid-term targets, capital allocation) is a pending catalyst NOT in the numbers; re-judge margin and growth paths after it. SBC-zero market: house and street bases coincide, band_position is null by construction.

equity_bridge.item: Provisions for pensions and other post-employment benefits (debt-like)
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 AR balance sheet, note 26; net of plan assets
FY2025 AR: total equity 4,348.6 less equity attributable to shareholders 4,314.1

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: 10yr revenue CAGR 3.9% (FY2015-FY2025) and equity 5yr CAGR 4.0%, haircut for a trough-to-trough view; 3yr CAGRs measure FY2022 peak to FY2025 trough and are not a trend
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (+4.0%) diverges >30% from EPS 5yr CAGR (-9.5%) and from 3yr revenue (-7.9%): FY2022 was a price-inflation peak (revenue 19.4bn, EPS 5.74) and FY2025 a trough with EUR 141.5m of impairments. CAGRs ending in FY2025 understate the through-cycle trend; CAGRs ending in FY2022 overstate it. Owner-FCF CAGR (-10.3% 5yr) is below reported (-8.0%) because lease principal grew from 114 to 149.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs use the owner-FCF series (OCF - capex - lease principal): FY2020 905.9, FY2022 550.1, FY2025 524.6. SBC is nil throughout so no SBC adjustment distorts the series.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +3.2%: H1 2026 sales flat (7,925 vs 7,941) with Q2 +10.2% and a 'continuously positive price trend' into Q3, so H2 ~+7%. FY2027-28 4% = ~2% IP growth + ~1% price + ~1% bolt-on M&A (Chem Tech, Airedale pace), fading to 2.5% nominal.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 8.2% = guidance midpoint op. EBITDA 1,400 less ~110 of recurring special items on ~15.66bn sales. Glide to 8.7% by FY2029 = post-IFRS16 mid-cycle 8.4% plus roughly a third of the EUR 200-250m incremental cost-out targeted through 2027 (the rest assumed competed away in Essentials).
base.wc_rationale: Distributor: working capital 1,893 = 12.5% of FY2025 sales (turnover 7.3x); growth consumes cash at ~12% of the revenue increase. Negative capture.
base.terminal_rationale: Cap 15x owner FCF for a cyclical distributor; terminal growth 2% nominal EUR.

bull.rationale: FY2026 at the top of guidance (1,450 op. EBITDA -> 8.5% post-special-items). Margin reaches FY2022-23 levels (9.2-9.5%) as the full cost-out lands, Specialties mix shifts toward Life Science and the CMD reinstates a bolt-on M&A cadence adding ~2pp/yr to growth.

bear.rationale: FY2026 lands at the bottom of guidance (1,350) with elevated special items (strategy projects, talc legal costs); the H1 2026 rebound proves price-driven and reverses as the Iran-war energy spike fades and tariffs bite; FY2027-28 sales stall and margin settles at FY2018-19 (pre-cost-out) levels of ~7.5% as cost savings are competed away in Essentials. Terminal cap 13x reflects a chronically Essentials-heavy, lower-growth mix.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2025 was the trough. FY2026 operating EBITDA lands near the twice-raised EUR 1,350-1,450m guidance midpoint; sales recover ~3% on price with H1 flat and H2 up high-single-digit. The EUR 300m run-rate cost programme plus EUR 200-250m incremental through 2027 lifts the post-special-items EBITDA margin from 8.0% to 8.7% by FY2029, roughly the post-IFRS16 mid-cycle plus a third of the targeted savings; the remainder is competed away in Essentials as it has been historically. Growth settles at ~4% (industrial production + price + bolt-ons) fading to 2.5%. Working capital absorbs ~12% of incremental sales. Dividend (EUR 1.90) is covered by owner FCF of ~EUR 3.7-5/share. The 12-Nov-2026 CMD is not modelled; a credible mid-term margin target above 9% would move the base toward the bull path.
scenario_narratives.bull: The chemical-distribution cycle turns decisively and the new CEO's simplification (two-member board, removal of a management layer, local sales empowerment) delivers the full cost-out into a recovering volume environment. Specialties grows faster than Essentials, pulling group mix toward IMCD/Azelis-like economics; margin reaches 9.5% (FY2022-23 levels) by FY2030 and the CMD reinstates a disciplined bolt-on M&A cadence worth ~2pp/yr of growth in a market management calls favourably priced. Terminal cap 16x.
scenario_narratives.bear: The H1 2026 rebound is a price pass-through from the Iran-war energy shock rather than volume, and reverses in FY2027 as crude normalises and US tariffs depress industrial production; Essentials prices deflate as they did in FY2025. The new management team, which has already missed twice in FY2025 and reversed the divisional split, cannot hold the cost savings against competitive pressure; margin settles at 7.5%, FY2018-19 territory. Talc successor-liability claims (Whittaker, Clark & Daniels) and strategy-project costs keep special items elevated. Leverage (3.1bn incl. leases, ~2.3x op. EBITDA) stays comfortably investment-grade so there is no solvency path, but the dividend is held flat and growth is nominal GDP at best. Terminal cap 13x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: both divisions missed guidance twice in FY2025, the management team is less than 18 months old, the planned divisional split was reversed, and the FY2026 rebound is so far one strong quarter plus a raised guide, with a large open question (the Nov-12 CMD) still ahead. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs the cycle, the cost-out AND an M&A/mix re-rating all to land together, in a business where Essentials (72% of sales) is commodity distribution with little pricing power. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Brenntag as a mid-cycle owner-FCF stream, not off the FY2025 trough and not off the FY2022 price-inflation peak. The margin path is anchored to FY2026 guidance and to the seven post-IFRS16 years of margins on a post-special-items basis, with lease cash charged once inside the flows and lease liabilities therefore excluded from net debt. Cyclicality is priced through scenario weights (25/50/25) rather than a WACC premium. SBC is nil, so house and street bases coincide. Terminal values are capped at 13-16x owner FCF because the market has not historically paid a compounder multiple for an Essentials-heavy distributor.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin assumption (8.7% base) depends on retaining roughly a third of the EUR 200-250m cost-out; if none is retained, base IV falls toward the bear case
FY2026 guidance (EUR 1,350-1,450m operating EBITDA) is the year-1 anchor; a Q3 (Nov-2026) miss or a CMD reset would move it
Net debt is taken at the seasonally high 30-Jun-2026 balance (EUR 460m H1 working-capital build); a year-end release would add ~EUR 2-3/share
Working-capital capture (-12% of revenue growth) is a material cash drag in the bull case and a tailwind in a revenue decline
Talc/product-liability and French antitrust tail risks are in the bear narrative, not quantified in the bridge
Capital Markets Day 12-Nov-2026: new strategy, mid-term targets and capital-allocation framework not yet reflected
